Tajweed pause symbols are placed above words to guide the reciter where to stop or continue, ensuring the sacred meaning remains preserved.
Marks the completion of a full thought or theme. Stopping here is highly recommended so that the next sentence can start cleanly.
Halting recitation here is compulsory. Continuing without stopping will alter or corrupt the intended divine meaning.
Stopping here is strictly forbidden because the sentence structure is not yet complete. If you run out of breath and must stop, repeat from the preceding word.
You have equal choice to stop or continue recitation; neither choice is preferred over the other.
Stopping is permissible, but connecting with the following word is preferred and superior in meaning.
Continuing is permissible, but pausing at this word is preferred and superior in meaning.
These three dots appear in pairs on nearby words. You may pause at ONE of the two places, but you must NEVER pause at both, nor skip both.
Make a momentary, brief pause in sound for approximately one count without drawing a new breath, then immediately resume recitation.
Marks the conclusion of an Ayah. Pausing at the end of each verse is the authentic Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
Indicates a verse of Sujood at-Tilawah (prostration of recitation). Performing one prostration upon reciting or hearing it is Sunnah Mu\'akkadah.
